To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

short-period InAs/ GaAs superlattics represent a quantum well of average In0.16 Ga0.84As with a slightly modulated band structure, and that the electron density can be tuned by changing the InAs thickness Q in the superlattice.

the optical and transport measurements of short-period superlatices of InAs in GaAs with a total thickness of only 14 nm show that the electron wavefunctions are not strongly modulated by the short period potential and the electron density is determined by the InAs layer.

the electron density can be controlled in a wide range by the InAs layer width, the photoluminescence peak energy and linewidth are determined by the number of periods, the Shub–nikov–de-Haas effect is observed in the range 1.5 ≤ Q ≤ 4.5 ML, the Hall mobility is in the range 6000–10,000 cm2/V s, and variable range hopping conductivity is found for Q ≥ 2 ML.

short-period InAs superlattics are good candidates to fabricate high mobility two-dimensional electron gases.
